conviction_note: 0 because no event could be confirmed for the 2026-09-28 session. KGL files only Appendix 5B quarterlies, and its next one is due about 30 October. The only scheduled document near this date is the FY26 annual report, due by 30 September. The three before it landed on 21 Sep 2023 (16:13, after the close), 24 Sep 2024 (10:59, in session) and 26 Sep 2025 (17:47, after the close), and the stock moved 0.0%, -1.0% and +3.6% (one tick) on them. The one real catalyst is the company's own Q3 CY2026 target for the final investment decision (FID) and contracts. That target expires on 30 Sep, outside this one-session window, so it is filed under outside_window.
bar: For a quarterly_report_only developer the bar is cash and runway plus what the company promised this quarter. The runway question is settled: A$25.43m cash at 30 June 2026 and 4.71 quarters of funding in the Appendix 5B, then about A$300m of equity completed on 24 Jul and 5 Aug, and the company calls itself fully funded. The live bar is the 'Q3 CY2026 Priorities' list: finalise the Sedgman process-plant EPC contract and the open-pit mining contract, approve FID, and commence site mobilisation (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260731/pdf/0728hwd429hnnh.pdf, 2026-07-31). FID for Q3 CY2026 was restated on 2026-08-19 (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260819/pdf/072xt5yk2c2jp3.pdf). The second US$16m tranche of the Wheaton early deposit is 'planned for late September 2026' (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260618/pdf/070rgmnz73gbp6.pdf). The bar is company-sourced, but the event date is not, so nothing is sized in-window.

outside_window.finding: Q3 CY2026 ends 30 Sep, and none of FID, the Sedgman EPC contract, the open-pit mining contract or Wheaton early-deposit tranche 2 has been announced. The company restated all of them for Q3 CY2026 on 31 Jul and 19 Aug. On 2026-09-25 the stock sat at A$0.185, 7.5% below the A$0.20 raise price, with no lodgement since 4 Sep. Resolution comes by 30 Sep: either an FID/contract announcement (modest positive) or the annual report's directors' report restating the timetable (modest negative for a slip). Nothing ties it to the 28 Sep session. The net sign leans slightly negative because the EPC contract, which normally precedes FID, is also still unannounced with three sessions left, but that is weak evidence.
